newsitem.title: USA: France may not need new 97 budget measures - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: France may not need new 97 budget measures - Arthuis.

text.p: France may be able to reach its target of reducing its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year without new measures, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Sunday.
But he noted that the finance ministry had nonetheless frozen some credit lines as a precaution to ensure that it can and will meet the three percent target this year.
"Public spending is under control. Our growth forecast of 2.3 percent is a cautious forecast," he told reporters after a meeting of Group of Seven finance ministers and central bankers.
Business investment remained tentative, but a decision by President Jacques Chirac to call an early two-round election on May 25 and June 1 would lift uncertainty and encourage investment.
"I think that we can meet the target without recourse to what you have suggested," he said, when asked whether France would need new measures to bring its deficit down this year.
"For the time being, I see nothing to justify it," he said.
